clue.text: Investigates frontless dresses

indicators.note: without its front: the first letter goes

parts.note: PROBES = investigates, minus its first letter P

explanation.surface: Someone is looking into dresses that have no front panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresses' reads as a verb beside 'investigates', but it is the plural noun, garments like robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes are long loose garments, a kind of dress.

clue.text: Item of fruit came up hard? One gets soft

indicators.note: the one takes the soft letter after it

parts.note: rose = came up, as the sun does

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit turned out hard, and then one goes soft.
explanation.walkthrough: The hard/soft contrast looks like a comment on ripeness, but both words are single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod a rose leaves after flowering is eaten or made into syrup, so botanically it counts as a fruit.

clue.text: Defender holding line in NZ colours?

parts.note: a back is a defender in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby defender wears the New Zealand kit and holds the line.
explanation.walkthrough: New Zealand's rugby team, the All Blacks, plays in black, hence the question mark on a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Black is the colour New Zealand's national sides wear.

clue.text: Unusual prison pictures revealing elevated characters

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Odd photographs from a jail show some high-ranking people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated characters' suggests important people, but the characters are letters written above the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Superscription is writing placed above, and superscript characters sit raised above the line.

clue.text: Quiet introduction of scale of temperature

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gentle start to a temperature scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' in the middle does double duty: it belongs to the indicator phrase and also appears in the answer as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and quiet both describe a low sound.

clue.text: Science, kind curtailed aboard ship (cutter)

indicators.note: its tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: SORT = kind, minus its last letter T

explanation.surface: A science and a sort of vessel are named, with a cutter, itself a type of boat, in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a small sailing ship, which the bracketed word leans on, but here it means something that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The bracketed word, which sounds like a boat, defines scissors by their only job: cutting.

clue.text: Closed down in the past, beset by US lawman

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A business shut down long ago while hounded by an American federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed is American slang for a federal agent, usually of the FBI, which is what makes him a US lawman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fold is the standard verb for a business going under, and folded matches closed down in tense.

clue.text: Mapmakers interrupted by recall of finished work

indicators.note: to be interrupted is to have something break into the middle

parts.note: OS = Ordnance Survey, the UK's national mapping agency

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Cartographers are distracted by a completed piece being recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished work' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'finished' is wordplay and 'work' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for work and names a single composition or book, often numbered in a catalogue.

clue.text: Composer favouring including acceptable arrangement for five

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of five into a new order
to include is to hold within

explanation.surface: A composer likes including a suitable arrangement for a quintet.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'arrangement for five' sounds like music scored for five players, which suits a composer, but it is an anagram of the word five.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sergei Prokofiev, the Russian who wrote Peter and the Wolf, is one composer.

clue.text: Flickering screen with unknown landscape

indicators.note: the letters flicker into a new order

parts.note: y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A flickering screen shows a view of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters like x, y and z stand for unknowns in algebra, which is how 'unknown' gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scenery and landscape both mean the view of natural surroundings.

clue.text: Lined beach and pier up? Impossible to work out

indicators.note: the letters are torn up and remade

parts.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters; 'and' just joins the parts

explanation.surface: A seafront lined with a beach and a pier is thrown into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks as if it belongs with 'pier', but it is the anagram indicator, in the sense of things being all broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indecipherable cannot be worked out or read.

clue.text: Quantity of current beginning to matter in motionless crushing machine

indicators.note: the beginning of matter is its first letter

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A measurement of electricity flows into a machine that has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: An ampere, the amp for short, is the unit of electric current, so a quantity of current is measured in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp mill crushes ore with heavy pounding stamps.

clue.text: Executioner's tool? Never sit to have head cut off!

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.words: sit to have head cut off
parts.note: POSE = sit (for a portrait), minus its first letter P

explanation.surface: A plea never to sit for the executioner, because heads get cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures beheading, the wrong method of execution for a noose; the question mark flags the grim joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The hangman's noose is the tool of an execution by hanging.

clue.text: One putting up alfresco holidaymaker?

definitions.meaning: one who hikes prices, putting them up
someone walking in the open air on holiday

explanation.surface: Someone pitching a tent on an outdoor holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' suggests a tent, but it means raising, as in a price hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker walks outdoors for pleasure, and one who hikes raises something.

clue.text: Dock worker to deserve being at sea?

indicators.note: confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Does a man who works the docks earn a place at sea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a dock worker's world, which hides its use as the anagram indicator meaning bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a dock.

clue.text: Conveyor of brief message after vehicle died

parts.note: d = died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A short note arrives after a car death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as the order of events, but here it is the prefix POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard carries a short message through the mail.

clue.text: Excellent and wise person producing big American event

parts.note: an owl is a byword for wisdom

explanation.surface: A brilliant, wise figure puts on a big show in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay breaks one letter later than the enumeration, so the solver must ignore the space in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the NFL's championship game, a huge American event.

clue.text: Criticise volume one? Biography cut short before end of story

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: LIFE = biography, minus its last letter E

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A reviewer pans the first volume of a biography that stops short of the story's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume one' reads as the first book of a set, but it splits into V and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to vilify is to speak ill of someone, the harshest end of criticising.

clue.text: American begged to follow vehicle on rails, getting run down

indicators.note: to follow is to come after

parts.note: pled is the American past tense of plead

explanation.surface: An American pleaded while chasing a tram, only to be knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' marks the US spelling: pled where British English says pleaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Run down, as by a vehicle or a stampede, means knocked over and crushed underfoot.

clue.text: Short time out to get family item for table

parts.note: a nap is a short rest

explanation.surface: A brief break lets the family fetch something for the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short time out' reads like a sports break, but it is a brief sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Table linen is where the napkin belongs, so the clue defines it by where it lives.

clue.text: A lot of birds felt sun shimmering

indicators.note: the letters waver into a new order

explanation.surface: A flock of birds feel the sun's shimmering heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of birds' sounds like a big flock, but a nestful is only as many as one nest holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestful is the brood of birds a nest holds.

clue.text: One runs from greatest opponent on record

indicators.note: one R, run, runs away from the word

parts.note: an arch-rival is your greatest opponent
one R (r = runs in cricket) leaves ARCHRIVAL

explanation.surface: An athlete runs away from their fiercest competitor, a record-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On record' reads like a sporting record, but it is the definition: kept in the archives.
explanation.definitionFit: Archival means kept on record in archives.

clue.text: Send up a lot of tough seafood

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to lob is to send a ball high up
STERN = tough, minus its last letter N

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a lot of the seafood is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' suggests mockery, but it means a lob, a high throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lobster is one of the shellfish sold and eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Urge competition — something seen with soldiers?

parts.note: a cup is a competition, like the FA Cup

explanation.surface: A contest is urged on, with something alongside the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast in British homes, dipped into a boiled egg standing in its eggcup; the question mark marks the pun on army soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggcup holds the boiled egg that toast soldiers are dipped into.

clue.text: Plan — an excellent idea? — to get behind beds

indicators.note: to get behind something is to go after it

parts.note: strata are layers or beds of rock
a gem of an idea is an excellent one

explanation.surface: A scheme: a clever notion about getting behind the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests furniture, but these are geological beds, layers of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stratagem is a cunning plan, originally a military one.

clue.text: What going into pub set back?

definitions.text: What going into pub set back?

indicators.note: going into something means entering it
to be set back is to be put backwards

explanation.surface: A question: what happens when drinking in pubs causes a setback?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rehab is what someone whose drinking has set them back goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab treats people whose lives have been set back by drink.

clue.text: Spirit? Try a touch of tequila

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

indicators.note: just a little of the word: its first letter

explanation.surface: Want a spirit? Try some tequila.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'tequila' paint a bar, but spirit means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of courage: to take heart or lose heart is to gain or lose spirit.

clue.text: Ring-bearer? Father the same, bearing ring

explanation.surface: A man at a wedding carries the ring, as his father did.
explanation.walkthrough: Frodo Baggins carries the One Ring in The Lord of the Rings; the surface suggests a wedding page.
explanation.definitionFit: Frodo is the hobbit who bears the Ring in Tolkien's story.

clue.text: Serviceperson's angry speech with VIP

parts.note: a rant is an angry speech

explanation.surface: A soldier's furious tirade in front of a dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceperson' suggests the armed forces; here the service is a church service, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the person who leads a religious service.

clue.text: Flower idly avoiding a zone

indicators.note: the word does without these letters

parts.note: A plus Z for zone, both removed from LAZILY

explanation.surface: A flower sits idly, keeping out of a particular area.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and Z from LAZILY leaves L-ILY.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lily is one flower among many, and the plain 'Flower' covers it.

clue.text: Wanting content soup used veg

indicators.note: without their contents, so only the outer letters stay

explanation.surface: Someone unhappy with their soup had vegetables put in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting content' sounds like a dissatisfied diner; it means lacking contents, the inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for potato, a vegetable.

clue.text: Go into American heartland, heading away

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and it goes away

parts.note: CENTER, the American spelling of centre, minus its first letter C

explanation.surface: Someone travels into the middle of the United States, then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' flags the US spelling CENTER, which loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enter a room is to go into it.
